title: Age of Discovery
summary: Columbus, da Gama, Cortes, Magellan-Elcano and Pizarro redraw the map of the world.

events.title: Columbus reaches the Americas
events.summary: The first Spanish crossing of the Atlantic makes landfall in the Bahamas.
events.body:
Sailing west from Palos under the Castilian crown, Columbus reached the Bahamas in October 1492, believing he had found a route to Asia.

The landfall opened sustained European contact with the Americas.

events.title: Vasco da Gama reaches India
events.summary: Portugal opens a sea route to India around the Cape of Good Hope.
events.body:
Da Gama rounded southern Africa and crossed the Indian Ocean to Calicut, establishing the first all-sea trade route between Europe and India.

It broke the overland spice monopoly and launched Portugal's maritime empire.

events.title: Cortes and the fall of Tenochtitlan
events.summary: A Spanish-led march inland topples the Aztec capital.
events.body:
Landing near Veracruz in 1519, Cortes marched inland, forging alliances with rivals of the Mexica.

After the siege of 1521, Tenochtitlan fell, opening central Mexico to Spanish rule.

events.title: Magellan-Elcano circumnavigation
events.summary: The first voyage around the globe, completed by Elcano.
events.body:
Magellan's expedition crossed the Atlantic, threaded the strait that bears his name, and reached the Pacific; Magellan died at Mactan in 1521.

Elcano brought the survivors home in 1522, proving the world could be circled by sea.

events.title: Pizarro and the conquest of Peru
events.summary: The Inca emperor is captured at Cajamarca.
events.body:
Pizarro advanced from Panama down the Pacific coast and inland to Cajamarca, where he seized the Inca ruler Atahualpa in 1532.

The campaign brought the Inca Empire under Spanish control within a few years.
